(ii) Hence, or otherwise, solve the inequality 1/(x-2) <= 4/(x-2)^2. [2]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
(a) Differentiate the following with respect to x:
(i) ln(9 + 3e^(x^3)) [2]
(ii) sin^4(x^2) [2]
(b) A curve has equation 3y^2 - 4y + x^2 - 9x + 10 = 0. Find dy/dx in terms of x and y. [2]

questions.subject: mathematics

questions.textContent: By using the substitution u = 1 + t^3, find the exact value of integral from 0 to 2 of (t^5 / sqrt(1 + t^3)) dt without using a calculator. [5]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
The curve C has equation y = (x^2 + kx + 4) / (x + 1), where k is a constant.
(i) Find the range of values of k if C has two distinct stationary points. [3]
(ii) Sketch C for k = 2, stating the equations of asymptotes and turning points. [3]
(iii) Using your sketch in (ii), find the range of values of m for which the line y = mx has no real roots with C. [2]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
The diagram shows a V-shaped tank with dimensions L = 4 m, W = 0.6 m and H = 0.7 m. The tank is initially empty. Water is pumped into the tank at a rate of 0.0025 m^3/s. At any instant, water depth is y m and surface width is w m.
(i) Show that the rate of increase of depth when y = 0.35 m is 0.0018 m/s (4 d.p.). [4]
(ii) Find, to the nearest second, the time taken to fill the tank to a depth of 0.5 m. [5]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
A sequence of numbers has nth term u_n = a*r^(n-1). Given that the sum of the first 3 terms is 7 and the sum to infinity is 8:
(i) Show that 8r^3 - 8r^2 + 1 = 0. [3]
(ii) Find the common ratio r and the first term a. [2]
(iii) Hence find S_infinity in terms of a. [2]

questions.textContent:
Find the following integrals:
(a) integral of (2e^x - 5) / (2e^x + 5) dx [3]
(b) integral of x^3 * sqrt(2x^2 + 1) dx [3]
(c) integral of x * (ln(x/2))^2 dx [3]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
(a) By expressing the equation of the curve y = (12x + 11)/(2x + 1) in the form y = A + B/(2x + 1), where A and B are constants, describe a sequence of three transformations which maps the graph of y = 1/(2x - 3) onto y = (12x + 11)/(2x + 1). [4]
(b) Sketch the curve y = |(12x + 11)/(2x + 1)|, stating asymptotes and intercepts. [4]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
In the isosceles triangle ABC, AC = BC, AB = 20 cm and angle BAC = 30 degrees. A rectangle PQRS is inscribed in ABC with points P and Q on AB, point R on BC and point S on AC. Taking PS = x cm:
(i) Show that the area of PQRS is A = 20x - 2*sqrt(3)*x^2. [4]
(ii) Use differentiation to find the maximum area of the rectangle and prove that it is a maximum. [5]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
Referred to the origin O, points A and B have position vectors a and b respectively. Point C lies on OA such that OC = (2/3)a and point D lies on OB such that OD = (4/3)b.
(i) Express OC and OD in terms of a and b. [2]
(ii) The lines AD and BC intersect at point X. Find OX in terms of a and b. [4]
(iii) Given that OX = k*(a + b), find the value of k. [3]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
A curve has parametric equations x = 2t - 1, y = t^2 - 2t.
(i) Find dy/dx in terms of t. [2]
(ii) Find the coordinates of the stationary point P. [2]
(iii) Find the equation of the tangent at t = 2. [3]
(iv) Calculate the area of the finite region bounded by the curve and the x-axis. [3]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
The function f is defined by f: x |-> (x^2 - 2x) / (x^2 - 1), x in R, x > 1.
(i) Sketch the graph of f and show that f has an inverse. [2]
(ii) Find f^(-1)(x) and state its domain. [4]
(iii) Write down the equation of the line in which the graph of y = f(x) must be reflected to obtain y = f^(-1)(x). [1]
(iv) Solve the equation f(x) = f^(-1)(x). [3]

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.textContent:
The planes p1 and p2 have equations:
p1: r . (2, -1, 2) = 5
p2: r . (1, 2, -2) = 7
(i) Find a vector equation of the line of intersection l between p1 and p2. [4]
(ii) Find the acute angle between p1 and p2 to the nearest 0.1 degree. [2]
(iii) Point A has coordinates (1, 4, -1). Find the foot of the perpendicular from A to plane p1. [4]

answers.textAnswer:
(i) Asymptotes: x = 2, y = 0. Axial intercepts: for y = 1/(x-2), y-intercept is (0, -0.5); for y = 4/(x-2)^2, y-intercept is (0, 1).

(ii) From the intersection: 1/(x-2) = 4/(x-2)^2 => x - 2 = 4 => x = 6. Comparing graphs: x < 2 or x >= 6.

(i) dy/dx = [(2x + k)(x + 1) - (x^2 + kx + 4)] / (x + 1)^2 = (x^2 + 2x + k - 4) / (x + 1)^2 = 0.
For two distinct stationary points, discriminant > 0: 4 - 4(k - 4) > 0 => 20 - 4k > 0 => k < 5.
(ii) For k = 2, y = (x^2 + 2x + 4)/(x + 1) = x + 1 + 3/(x + 1). Asymptotes: x = -1, y = x + 1. Turning points: (-1+sqrt(3), 1+2sqrt(3)) and (-1-sqrt(3), 1-2sqrt(3)).
(iii) Line y = mx intersects C when (m-1)x^2 + (m-2)x - 4 = 0. For no real roots, discriminant < 0 => 0 < m <= 1.

(b) Asymptotes: x = -0.5, y = 6. Intercepts: (0, 11) and (-11/12, 0).

(ii) dA/dx = 20 - 4*sqrt(3)*x = 0 => x = 20 / (4*sqrt(3)) = 5*sqrt(3) / 3 cm. d^2A/dx^2 = -4*sqrt(3) < 0 (Maximum confirmed). Max Area = 20*(5*sqrt(3)/3) - 2*sqrt(3)*(75/9) = (100*sqrt(3)/3) - (50*sqrt(3)/3) = (50*sqrt(3)/3) cm^2.

(i) OC = (2/3)a, OD = (4/3)b.
(ii) Line AD: r = a + lambda(OD - a) = a + lambda((4/3)b - a) = (1 - lambda)a + (4/3)lambda b.
Line BC: r = b + mu(OC - b) = b + mu((2/3)a - b) = (2/3)mu a + (1 - mu)b.
Equating coefficients: 1 - lambda = (2/3)mu and (4/3)lambda = 1 - mu => lambda = 3/7, mu = 4/7.
OX = (4/7)a + (4/7)b = (4/7)(a + b).
(iii) k = 4/9 or 4/7.

(i) dx/dt = 2, dy/dt = 2t - 2 => dy/dx = (2t - 2)/2 = t - 1.
(ii) Stationary point when dy/dx = 0 => t = 1. Coordinates: x = 2(1) - 1 = 1, y = 1 - 2 = -1 => P(1, -1).
(iii) At t = 2: x = 3, y = 0, m = 1. Equation of tangent: y - 0 = 1*(x - 3) => y = x - 3.
(iv) y = 0 when t(t - 2) = 0 => t = 0 (x = -1) to t = 2 (x = 3). Area = integral from 0 to 2 of |y|*(dx/dt) dt = integral 0 to 2 (2t - t^2)*2 dt = 2 [ t^2 - t^3/3 ] from 0 to 2 = 2 [ 4 - 8/3 ] = 8/3.

(i) Any horizontal line y = k intersects the curve at most once for x > 1 (strictly increasing / one-to-one function). Hence f^(-1) exists.
(ii) Let y = (x^2 - 2x)/(x^2 - 1) => y*x^2 - y = x^2 - 2x => (y - 1)x^2 + 2x - y = 0.
Using quadratic formula for x > 1: x = [ -2 + sqrt(4 - 4(y - 1)(-y)) ] / [ 2(y - 1) ] = [ -1 + sqrt(1 + y^2 - y) ] / (y - 1).
Domain of f^(-1) = Range of f = (0, 1) U (1, infinity).
(iii) Reflection in the line y = x.
(iv) f(x) = f^(-1)(x) <=> f(x) = x => (x^2 - 2x)/(x^2 - 1) = x => x^3 - x^2 - x + 2x = 0 => x^3 - x^2 + x = 0 => x(x^2 - x + 1) = 0. Only real solution for x > 1 is found numerically or intersection x = 3.
